task.description: WF-02 Step 3 for REQ-134, implementing CODE-DESIGNER's approved design (gate-passed at step1b) as real, compilable test code. No lib/ module changes -- the design assigns all implementation to test-support/test code, so Step 2a (ELIXIR-DEV) was skipped by the dispatching ORCH. Resubmission (rework 1 of 3) after step3b's FAIL on AC3's fixture-repeatability defect -- see gate_history below.
acceptance_criteria: a test obtains a genuine token from the running Keycloak and drives it through Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline end to end, with the real assertion output quoted
the token's signature is verified against the live JWKS via the real verifier, not TokenVerifierDouble -- demonstrated by the test failing if pointed at a tampered token
JIT provisioning creates a real user row on first authentication and reuses it on the second, asserted across two calls
the default mix test run still passes with Keycloak stopped, quoted as evidence
the real-token tests skip with a message naming exactly what must be running, rather than failing obscurely
the result states the exact command a developer runs to execute them

result.summary:
Rework 1/3, fixing step3b's BLOCKER: AC3's test in test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs asserted an absolute pre-call count of 0 for designer-user's JIT-provisioned row, but the design (S5) deliberately never tears down the bpm-default tenant/schema between invocations, and designer-user is a fixed seeded Keycloak identity with no per-run uniqueness available -- so the test passed on a database's first run and would fail deterministically on the second, against AC6's own documented command. Applied option (b), per ORCH's routed instruction and the validator's own stated preference: replaced the hardcoded 0/1/1 assertions with a baseline captured before either pipeline call (count_before = user_count_for_subject(schema_name, subject)), then asserted count_before + 1 after the first AuthPipeline.call/2 and still count_before + 1 (not + 2) after the second, keeping the user_id_1 == user_id_2 identity check unchanged. This makes the test correct on every invocation regardless of prior runs or other tests sharing the same persistent fixture, with no teardown added to a fixture the design deliberately keeps permanent. Updated test/specs/REQ-134.md's AC3 section (test-contract description, a new explicit 'why a baseline count, not a hardcoded 0' subsection recording the rework and its reasoning, and the bottom mutation-verification note) to match -- no remaining reference to a hardcoded-0 assertion anywhere in the spec.

No other file touched: KeycloakTestClient, the setup_all raise/message mechanism, the exclusion default (test/test_helper.exs), and AC1/AC2's tests are exactly as validated in the previous PASS-on-those-points gate -- per ORCH's routing instruction not to touch them, and independently confirmed unnecessary since the BLOCKER was scoped entirely to AC3's assertions.

mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force (MIX_ENV=test), re-run after the change: PASSED CLEAN -- 'Compiling 131 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app', zero warnings, zero errors.

AC4 default-exclusion, re-verified after the change (Keycloak still stopped): `mix test test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs` -> 'Excluding tags: [:keycloak]' / 'All tests have been excluded.' / 'Result: 0 tests, 3 excluded' -- unchanged from before the rework, as expected since the AC3 assertion change does not touch the exclusion mechanism.

AC5's raise-vs-skip mechanism is untouched by this rework and was already independently re-verified and ruled compliant by step3b -- no new evidence needed here.

Keycloak reachability in this environment: still NOT running (only postgres was Up via docker compose ps), unchanged from the prior submission -- AC1/AC2/AC3's live-Keycloak assertion output remains TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 job.

Developer command for AC6 (unchanged, re-verified accurate against the actual file path and @moduletag): mix test --include keycloak test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs

gate_history.summary: TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (step3b) independently re-verified AC1/AC2/AC4/AC6 and PASSED them, and independently re-derived AC5's raise-vs-{:skip} deviation as compliant with AC5's substance (two probe scripts confirming no ExUnit-native runtime skip path exists in this installed toolchain). The sole FAIL was a BLOCKER under checks (c)/(d) (fixture isolation / self-sufficiency): AC3's test asserted a hardcoded pre-call count of 0 for the seeded designer-user identity's JIT-provisioned row, but the design (S5) never tears down the permanent bpm-default tenant/schema between invocations and designer-user has no per-run-unique identity available -- so the test would pass on a database's first run and fail deterministically on every subsequent run of AC6's own documented command.
issues: AC3's test asserts an absolute pre-call count of 0 for a JIT-provisioned row keyed to a fixed, never-torn-down seeded identity (designer-user) against a permanent fixture schema -- fails deterministically on the second invocation of the suite against the same database.
gate_history.next_action: Rework TEST-DESIGNER: fix AC3's test repeatability defect, either by tearing down the designer-user row after the test or by rewriting the assertions to use a count captured before either pipeline call as a baseline (count_before, count_before+1, count_before+1), and reflect the fix in test/specs/REQ-134.md's AC3 section.
